label: prf:qou-exists-axiom-2
title: Proof of axiom 2 (observability) for QOU existence
html:
Take \mathfrak{g} = \mathfrak{sl}_2. Its adjoint representation is three-dimensional with weights 2, 0, -2 for the Cartan element H, so it is the irreducible highest-weight module V_1 of highest weight 2 (spin 1). At generic q the finite-dimensional type-1 modules of U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2) are classified by the same highest weights, and V_1 stays simple [kassel1995]. The unit object \mathbf{1} is the one-dimensional module of highest weight 0. Two simple modules with different highest weights are not isomorphic, so by Schur's lemma \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, V_1) = 0. \square

The claim concerns the adjoint representation of the Lie algebra (or of U_q(\mathfrak{g})), not the adjoint coaction of \mathcal{O}_q(G) on itself. By the Peter--Weyl decomposition \mathcal{O}_q(G) \cong \bigoplus_{\lambda} V_\lambda^{*} \otimes V_\lambda [woronowicz1988], each summand V_\lambda^{*} \otimes V_\lambda \cong \mathrm{End}(V_\lambda) carries the invariant \mathrm{id}_{V_\lambda}, so the invariants of that coaction are the class functions, one for each \lambda, and are not zero modulo the unit. The previous version of this proof argued the opposite.
